description:
`ln -s` and `cp` creating or preserving a symbolic link whose relative target climbs above the
agent's root. Only the link's text is stored, so the link is created, as in bash.

cases.name: symlink escape: ln -s creates a relative target that climbs above root
cases.script: mkdir w; cd w; ln -s ../../nonexistent-xyz esc; echo status=$?; readlink esc

cases.name: symlink escape: ln -sf replaces a file with such a link
cases.script: mkdir w; cd w; : > esc; ln -sf ../../nonexistent-xyz esc; echo status=$?; readlink esc

cases.name: symlink escape: ln -s into a directory creates one link per target
cases.script: mkdir w d; cd w; ln -s ../../a ../../b ../d; echo status=$?; readlink ../d/a ../d/b

cases.name: symlink escape: ln -s relative target that stays inside root still works
cases.script: mkdir -p w/a/b; cd w/a/b; ln -s ../../x safe; readlink safe; echo status=$?

cases.name: symlink escape: cp -s of a source above root fails
cases.script: mkdir w; cd w; cp -s ../../nonexistent-xyz esc; echo status=$?

expectedStderr.reason: fixture: both sides fail to stat the source -- the oracle reports a missing file, WASI refuses a path above the agent's root

cases.name: symlink escape: cp -a recreates a symlink's target text in a shallower directory
cases.script: mkdir -p a/b/c; cd a/b/c; ln -s ../x safelink; cd /; cp -a a/b/c/safelink shallow; echo status=$?; readlink shallow

cases.name: symlink escape: cp -a of the same symlink into a directory just as deep still works
cases.script: mkdir -p a/b/c d; ln -s ../x a/b/c/safelink; cp -a a/b/c/safelink d/; readlink d/safelink; echo status=$?
